not_found.note: The Internetwork traffic privacy page only lists connectivity options (VPN association, VPC associations); it does not say the path avoids the public internet. Facts used instead: Welcome page (bypassing internet service providers), remote_regions ('All networking traffic remains on the AWS global network backbone'), FAQ ('AWS Direct Connect bypasses the internet'). No fact claims the privacy page says it.

The protecting-data-in-transit overview page does not name VPN or IPsec. The sentence is on SEC09-BP02 (sec_protect_data_transit_encrypt): 'Consider using an IPsec VPN for securing point-to-point or network-to-network connections'. Fact: site-to-site-vpn-sec09-use-ipsec-vpn-for-network-to-network.

The page lists the allowed combinations (mutual + federated, mutual + Active Directory) as bullet fragments that are too short to quote. Facts quote the sentence 'a combination of mutual authentication with a user-based method' and 'both methods must then be used'.
The login banner is only described in the document-history table row (January 20, 2022); not added. Connection logging, self-service portal and Client Route Enforcement are added.

Default 40 seconds on docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/tunnel-configure ('You can specify 30 or higher. Default: 40'); quote spans two lines of the page, joined by a space. Fact site-to-site-vpn-dpd-timeout-default-40-seconds.

Concentrator date (2025-11-15 / 2025-11-19) and IPv6 outer tunnel date (2025-07-01) are change facts; not added here. Concentrator bandwidth and routes are added (site-to-site-vpn-concentrator-aggregate-5-gbps-site-100-mbps).
Hosted connection speeds (500 Mbps) are in the numbers lens fact direct-connect-limit-hosted-port-speeds; partner provisioning is in direct-connect-hosted-connection-provisioned-by-partner.

source_contradictions: Client VPN device posture: the guide (what-is, device-posture, limits) says Client VPN can grant access by device health with CrowdStrike, Jamf and JumpCloud, but the VPN FAQ (www/vpn/faqs) still answers 'No. AWS Client VPN does not support posture assessment.' The feature has no date in the document history or the What's New feeds, so it is not examinable until a date is found. Fact client-vpn-device-posture-controls-access-by-device-health has volatility frequently-changing; the FAQ answer was not turned into a fact.

VPN backup for critical workloads: the whitepaper cost page says AWS does not recommend Direct Connect with an internet VPN backup for highly critical or critical workloads, while the Direct Connect resiliency page says to consider a Site-to-Site VPN on a transit gateway as a backup for mission critical workloads and the Well-Architected page calls it a cost-effective backup. The writer should present: VPN backup is cheaper but limited to 1.25 Gbps per tunnel; ECMP on a transit gateway raises it; Direct Connect with a second connection remains the most resilient.

Direct Connect gateway and VPC-to-VPC traffic: the FAQ says a Direct Connect gateway only routes between virtual interfaces and virtual private gateways; the guide (direct-connect-gateways-intro) adds a November 2021 exception for a supernet advertised on one virtual interface. The fact quotes the guide with the exception.
Concentrator gateways: the demand text said transit gateway or Cloud WAN; the guide says VPN Concentrators are only supported with Transit Gateway, not Cloud WAN or virtual private gateway.
